question.problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ at the point $A(4,3)$ in the direction towards the point $B(1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The directional derivative ${f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)$ of a function $f(x,y)$ at the point $(a,b)$ in the direction of the vector $v$ is given by

$$
{f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)=∇f(a,b)\cdot u
$$

where $u$ is a unit vector in the direction of $v.$

First, we find the direction vector and the corresponding unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,1⟩-⟨4,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-2⟩ \\ u & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}}{‖\overset{\to }{AB}‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}}⟨-3,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}⟨-3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the gradient $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $A(4,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}},\,\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}⟩ \\ ∇f(4,3) & =⟨\frac{4}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}}},\,\frac{3}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4}{5},\frac{3}{5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the directional derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{u}^{′}(4,3) & =∇f(4,3)\cdot u \\  & =⟨\frac{4}{5},\frac{3}{5}⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}},-\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{4(-3)+3(-2)}{5\sqrt{13}} \\  & =-\frac{18}{5\sqrt{13}}.\end{aligned}
$$
